lede: The sharpest item this week is the San Miguel County BOCC's special meeting Wednesday, where they'll sit as the Housing Authority and vote on Resolution 2026-34 — a change to Area Median Income limits for deed-restricted units at Pinion Park, the kind of technical adjustment that quietly determines who actually qualifies for affordable housing here. Also worth watching: the County Planning Commission takes up three Land Use Code amendments Thursday covering forestry, oil and gas, and geothermal energy, all headed toward the BOCC if recommended. Meanwhile, the Film Festival crowd is clearing out and the valley is settling back into fall.

notable.stake: BOCC votes on AMI limits that determine who qualifies for Pinion Park deed-restricted housing.
Planning Commission weighs in on three Land Use Code changes before they advance to BOCC.
